qualitative_samples.title: nullspan structured extraction launch
qualitative_samples.draft: Baked nullspan a single-pass structured extraction with exact [start, end] character spans, calibrated p_null abstention, algebraic invariant checks (subtotal == nodes * hourly_rate), and p10/p50/p90 quantiles.
qualitative_samples.zerodep_rewrite:
Meet nullspan: a structured extraction engine that pulls exact `[start, end]` spans from text, knows when a value isn't there instead of making one up (`p_null`), and double-checks the math (`subtotal == nodes * hourly_rate`).

You can run it three ways:
- ⚡ Full neural model (PyTorch, 67M): 98.8% overall — 100% on structured & math checks, 91.7% on SQuAD v2.0, and 100% at spotting unanswerable prompts.
- 🌐 Browser-native (64 MB WASM): 4× smaller quantized model running entirely in the browser with 90% SQuAD v2.0 accuracy.
- 🚀 Zero-dependency JS/Python (0 MB): Deterministic lexical + AST math engine — 100% on structured logs/invoices in 0.005 ms.

qualitative_samples.title: Skills vs MCP for AI Agents
qualitative_samples.draft: In contemporary artificial intelligence agent architectures, practitioners often debate whether modular Skill definitions supersede the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
qualitative_samples.zerodep_rewrite:
Skills vs MCP? Wrong question.

Both are tools for building AI agents. But they solve different problems:
- Skills = what your agent knows how to do
- MCP = what your agent can access

One teaches. One connects. You need both.
